chapters.title: Family and Describing People
chapters.goal: Family words, tener, describing words that match, my/your/our, -er and -ir verbs.

lessons.title: My Family
lessons.goal: Name the people in your family.

sections.title: Mixed groups
sections.body: For a group with at least one male, Spanish uses the -os word. Los hermanos can mean "the brothers" or "brothers and sisters." Los padres means "the parents."

lessons.title: To Have: Tener
lessons.goal: Say what you have, your age, and what you have to do.

sections.title: tener (to have) on the T-chart

rows.say: él tiene, ella tiene, usted tiene
ellos tienen, ellas tienen, ustedes tienen

sections.note: Look at the orange cells: the e turns into ie in four forms. Nosotros and vosotros keep the e. The yo form is odd: tengo.

sections.title: Saying your age
sections.body:
Spanish says you "have" years.
English: I am 20 years old. → Spanish: Tengo veinte años.
English: How old are you? → Spanish: ¿Cuántos años tienes?

sections.title: Tener que
sections.body:
Tener que + an action word means "to have to."
English: I have to study. → Spanish: Tengo que estudiar.

sections.title: Bonus: venir (to come)

rows.say: él viene, ella viene, usted viene
ellos vienen, ellas vienen, ustedes vienen

sections.note: Venir works just like tener: vengo, then e turns into ie.

quiz.p: How do you say "I'm 20 years old"?
How do you say "I have to study"?

lessons.title: Describing People
lessons.goal: Describe people with words that match.

sections.title: Words that match
sections.body:
Describing words match the person or thing: male or female, one or more than one. They usually come after the noun.
English: a tall boy → Spanish: un chico alto
English: a tall girl → Spanish: una chica alta
English: tall boys → Spanish: chicos altos
English: tall girls → Spanish: chicas altas

sections.title: Use ser to describe
sections.body: What someone is like uses ser: Ella es simpática. You learned ser in Chapter 2.

quiz.p: Where does the describing word usually go?
o: at the end of the sentence

quiz.p: How do you say "My brother is tall"?

t.p: Type "hard-working" for a group of women.

lessons.title: My, Your, Our
lessons.goal: Say whose something is.

sections.title: Whose is it?
head: English
One thing
More than one
sections.note: Vuestro is only used in Spain.

sections.title: Match the thing, not the owner
sections.body:
These words match the thing you own, not the person who owns it.
English: my brothers → Spanish: mis hermanos
English: our house → Spanish: nuestra casa
English: our books → Spanish: nuestros libros

sections.title: tu or tú?
sections.body: Tu (no accent) means "your." Tú (with an accent) means "you." Tu libro = your book. Tú tienes = you have.

sections.title: Whose? The "de" way
sections.body:
Spanish has no apostrophe s. Use de.
English: Ana's house → Spanish: la casa de Ana
English: his sister → Spanish: su hermana, or la hermana de él

lessons.title: Action Words: -er and -ir Verbs
lessons.goal: Use regular -er and -ir verbs.

sections.title: Same idea, new endings
sections.body: Chop off -er or -ir and add the ending. The two groups are the same except for nosotros and vosotros.

sections.title: comer (to eat) on the T-chart

rows.say: él come, ella come, usted come
ellos comen, ellas comen, ustedes comen

sections.note: The left side is one person. The right side is more than one. The gray row is only used in Spain.

sections.title: vivir (to live) on the T-chart

rows.say: él vive, ella vive, usted vive
ellos viven, ellas viven, ustedes viven

sections.note: Vivir matches comer except vivimos (we live) and vivís (you all, Spain).

sections.title: Examples
sections.body:
English: We eat at home. → Spanish: Comemos en casa.
English: Where do you live? → Spanish: ¿Dónde vives?
English: They read a lot. → Spanish: Leen mucho.
English: I write emails. → Spanish: Escribo correos.

quiz.p: How do you say "Where do you live?"

lessons.title: My Home
lessons.goal: Name the rooms of a home and say what is there.

sections.title: Different words, same room
sections.body: A bedroom can also be "la habitación" or "el cuarto," and Mexico often says "la recámara." All are fine.

quiz.p: How do you say "I live in an apartment"?

lessons.title: Optional: Spanish Names
lessons.goal: Understand Spanish last names and nicknames.

sections.title: Two last names
sections.body:
Many Spanish speakers have two last names: the first from the father, the second from the mother.
Example: Ana García López. García is from her father, López from her mother. Day to day she may just say Ana García.

quiz.p: In "Ana García López," García comes from...
A common nickname for José is...

lessons.title: Optional: Pronunciation Traps
lessons.goal: Hear the difference in words that are easy to mix up.

sections.title: Listen closely
sections.body: These pairs differ by one sound or one stress. Tap each one and compare.

sections.title: Watch the ñ
sections.body: Pena (a pity) and peña (a group of friends) are different words, so the ñ really matters. That is why typing n for ñ is never accepted here.

chapters.title: Free Time and Around Town
chapters.goal: Places in town, ir, making plans, verbs that change inside, odd yo forms.

lessons.title: Places Around Town
lessons.goal: Name places in town and say where things are.

sections.title: False friend
sections.body: La librería is a bookstore, not a library. A library is la biblioteca.

items.es: El banco está cerca del parque.
items.en: The bank is near the park.
items.sl: ehl BAHN-koh ehs-TAH SEHR-kah dehl PAHR-keh

sections.title: de + el = del
sections.body:
When de comes before el, they join into del.
English: next to the bank → Spanish: al lado del banco
De la does not join: al lado de la tienda.

quiz.a: El banco está cerca del parque.
o: El banco está cerca del parque.
El banco está lejos del parque.
El parque está al lado del banco.
quiz.audio: El banco está cerca del parque.

lessons.title: Going Places: Ir
lessons.goal: Say where you are going.

sections.title: ir (to go) on the T-chart

rows.say: él va, ella va, usted va
ellos van, ellas van, ustedes van

sections.note: Ir does not follow any pattern. Learn it by heart. Yo voy, tú vas.

sections.title: a + el = al
sections.body:
Ir goes with a (to). When a comes before el, they join into al.
English: I'm going to the park. → Spanish: Voy al parque.
English: We are going to the store. → Spanish: Vamos a la tienda.

sections.title: Where to vs where
sections.body: ¿Adónde? asks "where to?" with movement. ¿Dónde? asks "where?" for a place.

quiz.p: How do you say "Where are you going?"

lessons.title: Making Plans: Ir a + Verb
lessons.goal: Talk about what you are going to do.

sections.title: The easy future
sections.body:
Use ir + a + an action word to say what you are going to do.
English: I'm going to eat. → Spanish: Voy a comer.
English: We're going to study tomorrow. → Spanish: Vamos a estudiar mañana.
English: What are you going to do? → Spanish: ¿Qué vas a hacer?

items.en: What are you going to do?

sections.title: Do not forget the "a"
sections.body: Voy a comer, not "Voy comer." The little a is always there.

quiz.p: How do you say "I'm going to eat"?
How do you ask "What are you going to do?"

t.p: Type "I'm going to study" in Spanish.

lessons.title: Free Time and Sports
lessons.goal: Talk about hobbies and sports.

sections.title: Two kinds of "play"
sections.body: Jugar is for games and sports. Tocar is for instruments.

items.en: What do you like to do?

quiz.p: How do you say "to watch a movie"?

lessons.title: Verbs That Change Inside
lessons.goal: Use verbs whose middle vowel changes: e to ie, o to ue, e to i.

sections.title: The boot
sections.body: Some verbs change the vowel in the middle in four forms. If you circle those forms on the T-chart, they make a boot shape. Nosotros and vosotros stay outside the boot and do not change.

sections.title: querer (to want) on the T-chart

rows.say: él quiere, ella quiere, usted quiere
ellos quieren, ellas quieren, ustedes quieren

sections.note: e turns into ie inside the boot (the orange cells).

sections.title: poder (can, to be able to) on the T-chart

rows.say: él puede, ella puede, usted puede
ellos pueden, ellas pueden, ustedes pueden

sections.note: o turns into ue inside the boot.

sections.title: pedir (to ask for, to order) on the T-chart

rows.say: él pide, ella pide, usted pide
ellos piden, ellas piden, ustedes piden

sections.note: e turns into i inside the boot.

quiz.p: Which forms stay outside the boot?

lessons.title: Odd Yo Forms
lessons.goal: Learn verbs that are only odd in the yo form.

sections.title: Only yo is different
sections.body: These verbs are regular everywhere except the yo form. Learn the yo form and you are done.

sections.title: hacer (to do, to make) on the T-chart

rows.say: él hace, ella hace, usted hace
ellos hacen, ellas hacen, ustedes hacen

sections.note: Only the yo form (orange) is odd: hago.

quiz.p: How do you say "I don't know"?

lessons.title: Getting Around
lessons.goal: Talk about getting around town and asking the way.

sections.title: Car words
sections.body: Latin America often says el carro. Spain says el coche. Many places say el auto.

items.en: How do I get to the museum?

quiz.p: How do you say "to the left"?
How do you ask "How do I get to the museum?"
In Spain, a car is usually...

lessons.title: Optional: Saber or Conocer?
lessons.goal: Choose the right "to know."

sections.title: Two ways to know
head: Verb
Use it for
Example
rows: facts, information, how to do something
Sé nadar. (I know how to swim.)

sections.title: The personal a
sections.body: When the thing you know is a person, add a: Conozco a Ana. This little a is used before people after many verbs.

items.en: Do you know where it is?

lessons.title: Optional: Reading Signs
lessons.goal: Read common signs around town.

sections.title: Pull in Spain
sections.body: In Spain, "pull" is usually Tire, and in many places you will see Hale. Jale is common in Mexico and the US.

chapters.title: Weather, Feelings and Trips
chapters.goal: Months, weather, estar for feelings, the -ing form, ser or estar, lo and la.

lessons.title: Months and Dates
lessons.goal: Say the months, seasons and dates.

sections.title: Saying the date
sections.body:
Spanish puts the day first, then de, then the month.
English: May 5 → Spanish: el cinco de mayo
English: Today is March 10. → Spanish: Hoy es el diez de marzo.
For the first of the month, many people say el primero: el primero de enero.

items.sl: kwahl ehs lah FEH-chah deh oy

items.es: Hoy es el diez de marzo.
items.sl: oy ehs ehl dyehs deh MAHR-soh

sections.title: Small letters again
sections.body: Months start with a small letter in Spanish, just like days.

lessons.title: What's the Weather Like?
lessons.goal: Talk about the weather.

sections.title: Hace for most weather
sections.body:
Spanish uses hace (it makes) for most weather: Hace calor, Hace frío.
Rain and snow are their own verbs: Llueve, Nieva.
Compare: Hace frío (the weather is cold) and Tengo frío (I feel cold).

sections.title: Temperatures
sections.body: Most Spanish-speaking countries use Celsius. 30 degrees Celsius is hot, about 86 in Fahrenheit.

quiz.p: How do you ask "What's the weather like?"

lessons.title: How I Feel: Estar + Feelings
lessons.goal: Say how you feel right now.

sections.title: Feelings use estar
sections.body:
How you feel right now uses estar. The feeling word matches the person.
English: I'm tired. → Spanish: Estoy cansado. (a man) / Estoy cansada. (a woman)
English: We're happy. → Spanish: Estamos contentos.

sections.title: Angry in Spain
sections.body: In Spain, angry is usually enfadado / enfadada.

quiz.p: Nosotros estamos ___ (happy, a group of men).
How do you say "Are you OK?"

lessons.title: Right Now: The -ing Form
lessons.goal: Say what is happening right now.

sections.title: Estar + -ando / -iendo
sections.body:
To say what is happening right now, use estar + the -ing form.
-ar verbs: hablar → hablando
-er and -ir verbs: comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo
English: I'm eating. → Spanish: Estoy comiendo.
English: What are you doing? → Spanish: ¿Qué estás haciendo?

sections.title: Making the -ing form
head: Verb
-ing form
English
sections.note: Leer becomes leyendo, and dormir becomes durmiendo. These two are a little odd.

sections.title: Only for right now
sections.body: Spanish uses this only for things happening at this moment. For plans, use ir a: Voy a comer mañana, not "Estoy comiendo mañana."

lessons.title: Ser or Estar?
lessons.goal: Choose between the two verbs for "to be."

sections.title: Which one?
head: Use ser for
Use estar for
rows: who or what someone is: Soy estudiante.
where something is: Estoy en casa.
what someone is like: Es alta.
where someone is from: Es de México.
what is happening now: Está comiendo.
time and dates: Son las dos.
how something is right now: La sopa está fría.

sections.title: A memory trick
sections.body: How you feel and where you are, that is when you use estar.

sections.title: Same word, new meaning
sections.body:
Some describing words change meaning.
English: He is boring. → Spanish: Es aburrido.
English: He is bored. → Spanish: Está aburrido.
English: She is good (a good person). → Spanish: Es buena.
English: She is well. → Spanish: Está bien.

t.p: Type "I am a student" in Spanish.

lessons.title: It and Them: Lo, La, Los, Las
lessons.goal: Replace a thing or person with a short word.

sections.title: Short words for "it" and "them"
sections.body:
Instead of repeating a noun, use lo, la, los or las. They go right before the verb.
English: I buy the book. I buy it. → Spanish: Compro el libro. Lo compro.
English: I see the house. I see it. → Spanish: Veo la casa. La veo.

sections.title: With two verbs
sections.body:
With ir a or other two-verb sentences, you can also stick it on the end of the action word.
English: I'm going to buy it. → Spanish: Lo voy a comprar. or Voy a comprarlo.

sections.title: People too
sections.body: Lo and la also mean him and her: La conozco (I know her).

quiz.p: Where do lo and la usually go?
Which also means "I'm going to buy it"?

lessons.goal: Talk about travel plans.

sections.title: Ticket in Spain
sections.body: In Spain, a ticket is usually el billete.

sections.title: Trip talk
lines: What are you going to do in July?

lessons.title: Optional: A Peek at the Past Tense
lessons.goal: A short, no-pressure look at how to say what you did yesterday (hablé, comí).

sections.title: Just a peek
sections.body:
This is a preview of Spanish 102. Nothing here is required. It shows how to say what you did.
English: Yesterday I spoke with Ana. → Spanish: Ayer hablé con Ana.
English: I ate tacos. → Spanish: Comí tacos.

sections.title: hablar in the past (I spoke, you spoke...)

rows.say: él habló, ella habló, usted habló
ellos hablaron, ellas hablaron, ustedes hablaron

sections.note: Look at the accents on hablé and habló. They change the meaning: hablo means "I speak," but habló means "he spoke."

sections.title: comer in the past (I ate, you ate...)

rows.say: él comió, ella comió, usted comió
ellos comieron, ellas comieron, ustedes comieron

sections.note: -er and -ir verbs share these endings: comí, viví, escribí.

sections.title: Coming in 102
sections.body: The full past tense, with its odd verbs, comes in Spanish 102. For now, just enjoy hearing it.

o: I am going to eat tacos.
